segments.script: First, meaning. I read “that you have ordered a good dinner today, because I have reason to expect an addition to our family party” slowly and put it in my own words: Mr. Bennet tells his wife at breakfast to order a good dinner because he expects a guest. Next, craft. I notice his playful mystery, making her guess who is coming. The strongest word is “addition”: it is vague, which builds suspense. Then, effect. What is Mr. Bennet teasing his wife about? My answer: Mr. Bennet is teasing his wife about a mystery guest for dinner, enjoying her curiosity; the guest turns out to be Mr. Collins, the heir of the entail.
